# 1\. Executive Summary

This document defines Module 03 - Daily Tracker for the AMR Coordinator Portal (Placement Operations Management System / POMS), following the same structure established in Module 01 and Module 02. It reflects nine rounds of detailed workflow discussion and captures every finalized business and system-behaviour decision, including several points where the initial recommendation was deliberately revised after being tested against the coordinator's real daily workflow.

Module 03 is the coordinator's primary daily workspace - the module used every single working day to record calls, and the one that all other reporting modules ultimately depend on. If Module 02 (Master Company Database) is the brain of the system, the Daily Tracker is its heartbeat.

# 2\. Purpose

The Daily Tracker is the coordinator's primary workspace for recording and managing daily placement calls. Each calendar month is represented as one tracker (e.g. "July Tracker 2026"), and each working day within it is recorded, saved, and submitted as a discrete unit of work.

# 3\. Objectives

- Give each coordinator a fast, Excel-familiar workspace for making and recording ~50-70 calls per day.
- Load working contacts directly from the Master Company Database without manual copy-paste.
- Automatically and accurately track call start time, end time, and duration with minimal manual effort.
- Record only today's call outcome - not the full multi-day placement lifecycle.
- Feed positive outcomes into the Weekly Tracker (Module 04) automatically.
- Preserve incomplete work (No Response / Follow Up contacts) for optional continuation the next day.

# 4\. Daily Workflow Overview

A coordinator's day follows this sequence:

- Login → Daily Tracker.
- The tracker opens empty each day (no leftover unsaved data from the previous day - the previous day is always fully saved and submitted).
- Coordinator clicks Load Today's Contacts and selects working contacts for the day.
- Calls are made one row at a time; start time, end time, duration, call outcome, and comments are recorded per row.
- Rows auto-save as they are completed; the coordinator may also save manually.
- At the end of the day, the coordinator clicks Submit Day.
- Positive outcomes automatically flow into the Weekly Tracker.

A coordinator may also review any previous day's completed tracker via a calendar/date selector, purely for reference - this history view does not reopen the day for editing as an active session.

# 5\. Loading Today's Contacts

This was the single most-debated design decision in Module 03 and went through three iterations before being finalized.

## 5.1 Rejected Approach - Typing Company Names

The original idea (typing the first three letters of a company name to search, as used in Module 02) was rejected for the Daily Tracker. Coordinators do not know in advance which companies they will call - they instead pick a working set from the Master Company Database at the start of the day, so a name-based search does not fit this use case.

## 5.2 Rejected Approach - Full Master Database Page

Opening the entire Master Company Database screen to select contacts was also rejected, because it would let coordinators accidentally start editing or deleting master records while simply trying to prepare today's calls.

## 5.3 Final Design - Read-Only Contact Picker

Clicking Load Today's Contacts opens a read-only picker view of the Master Company Database:

- Available: checkbox selection of any contacts, Select All, and Load Selected Contacts.
- Not available in this view: Add, Edit, Delete, Export - these remain exclusive to Module 02.
- The coordinator may select any number of contacts (commonly ~70) entirely at their own discretion; there is no forced assignment or sequence.
- A shortcut link (Open Master Company Database) is available for the rare case where a coordinator needs to add a brand-new contact before loading it.

Selected contacts populate the Daily Tracker grid with Company Name, HR Name, Mobile Number, and Email ID pre-filled; Start Time, End Time, Duration, Call Outcome, and Comments remain empty and fully editable.

# 6\. New Contacts Received From a Team Leader

Team Leaders occasionally hand over additional contacts (commonly via WhatsApp) that are not yet in the Master Company Database. This flow is deliberately kept outside full automation:

- The coordinator (or Team Leader/Administrator) first adds these new contacts into the Master Company Database (Module 02) - manually typed or pasted.
- The Daily Tracker includes a Synchronize / Refresh control; after saving in the Master Database, the Daily Tracker's contact picker reflects the update within roughly one to five minutes, even against a 10,000+ row database.
- Once synchronized, the coordinator loads the new contact(s) into today's tracker exactly like any other contact via Load Today's Contacts.
- If a Team Leader sends additional contacts mid-day (e.g. 20 more at 2 PM, after 70 are already loaded), they are simply appended at the bottom of the current day's list (rows 71, 72, 73…) rather than opened in a separate merge popup - this was chosen for simplicity and because there is no fixed daily contact ceiling.

# 7\. Call Order & Duplicate Prevention Within the Day

- There is no system-assigned calling order or forced sequence - coordinators choose which loaded contact to call next, matching current practice.
- Contacts already worked with a final/closed outcome should not normally be repeated on the same day; contacts in Follow Up, Call Back, or No Response status may legitimately be tried again - this is not treated as a duplicate.
- If the same HR contact is loaded into today's tracker twice, the system displays a warning: "Already exists in today's tracker - do you want to skip?"
- Two contacts are only treated as genuinely distinct - and therefore not blocked - if at least one of HR Name, Mobile Number, or Email ID differs; Mobile Number is the highest-priority distinguishing field.

# 8\. Skip Functionality

Coordinators may decide mid-day that a loaded company should not be called again. Rather than displaying a Skip control on every row, the coordinator selects the specific row and clicks a single Skip button.

- The skipped row is removed from today's active tracker view.
- The record itself is not deleted from the Master Company Database - Skip is a Daily Tracker-only action, not a database action.

# 9\. Daily Tracker Grid - Final Columns

| **Column**                | **Behaviour**                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Serial No.                | System-generated, sequential for the day                            |
| Start Time                | Manual entry, or Spacebar / ⏱ Now to insert current system time     |
| End Time                  | Automatic - captured the moment Call Outcome is selected; read-only |
| Duration                  | Automatic - End Time minus Start Time; read-only                    |
| Company Name              | Pre-filled from the selected contact                                |
| HR Name                   | Pre-filled from the selected contact                                |
| Mobile Number             | Pre-filled from the selected contact; mandatory                     |
| Email ID                  | Pre-filled if available; optional - see Section 12                  |
| Call Outcome (Response 1) | Mandatory before the row can be considered complete                 |
| Comments                  | Optional free text                                                  |

Note: an earlier draft carried a separate "Response 2" column for secondary business status (e.g. Invite Sent, JD Received, Drive Scheduled). This was deliberately removed from the Daily Tracker - see Section 13.

# 10\. Time Tracking System (Final)

Time tracking went through several iterations - automatic-on-row-select and automatic-on-cell-click approaches were both tried and rejected before the final hybrid model was reached.

## 10.1 Time Format

A single format is used throughout the application: HH:MM:SS AM/PM - for example 10:35:25 AM. This avoids the ambiguity of any custom shorthand notation.

## 10.2 Start Time - Manual (Editable)

- The coordinator enters Start Time either by typing it directly, or by pressing Spacebar (or clicking a small ⏱ Now icon) while the cell is focused, which inserts the current system time instantly.
- Start Time remains fully editable at any point - important because coordinators take breaks, attend meetings, or get interrupted between loading a row and actually starting the call.

## 10.3 End Time - Automatic (Locked)

- End Time is never entered manually. The instant the coordinator selects a Call Outcome, the system captures the current system time as End Time and locks the field.

## 10.4 Duration - Automatic

- Duration = End Time − Start Time, calculated automatically and displayed in a readable form such as "01m 53s" rather than 00:01:53.

## 10.5 Design Rationale

Two earlier proposals were explicitly rejected: (1) auto-starting the timer the moment a row is opened/clicked - rejected because coordinators may pause before dialing, corrupting the duration; and (2) auto-carrying the previous row's End Time forward as the next row's Start Time - rejected because breaks and interruptions between calls would make the carried-over time inaccurate. The team also clarified that "Call Duration" in this system means activity duration (time to complete the call and log its outcome), not telephony-measured talk time, since coordinators dial from their personal mobile phones outside the software; true talk-time would require telephony integration, which is out of scope for v1.0.

## 10.6 Validation

If a coordinator selects a Call Outcome without an entered Start Time, the system blocks the save and displays: "Start Time is required before selecting Call Outcome. Press Spacebar to insert the current system time, or manually enter the Start Time." No row is allowed to reach a completed state without a Start Time, End Time, and Duration.

# 11\. Keyboard Shortcuts (Version 1.0)

Available only within the Daily Tracker while the coordinator is actively working on calls; they do not affect other modules.

| **Key**  | **Function**                                                           | **Notes**                                |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Spacebar | Fill the Start Time cell with the current system time (HH:MM:SS AM/PM) | Active only in Start Time cell           |
| Tab      | Move to the next editable cell                                         | Standard grid navigation                 |
| Enter    | Save the current row (Auto Save) and move to the next row              | Cursor lands on next row's Start Time    |
| Ctrl + S | Manual Save of the entire tracker                                      | In addition to per-row auto-save         |
| Delete   | Clear the selected editable cell (where permitted)                     | Not permitted on system-generated fields |

Design principle: the coordinator should never need to perform an unnecessary click. The intended hands-on-keyboard cycle is Space → Call → Outcome → (Comments) → Enter → Space → …, repeated 70+ times a day.

# 12\. Call Outcome (Response 1) & Removal of Response 2

Response 1 and Response 2 were originally designed together as Primary Call Outcome and Secondary Business Status. After walking through a real example (Invite Mail → Invite Sent → Awaiting JD, spanning several days after Submit Day had already been clicked), it became clear that Response 2 does not belong in the Daily Tracker at all, because the Daily Tracker only records what happened during today's call - it does not reopen previously submitted days to update a status days later.

Final decision: Response 1 is renamed Call Outcome and is the only outcome field retained in the Daily Tracker. The full secondary lifecycle (Invite Sent, Awaiting JD, JD Received, Drive Scheduled, Drive In Progress, Round 1/2/3, Awaiting Offers, Drive Completed) is deferred entirely to Module 04 - Weekly Tracker.

| **Call Outcome (Response 1)** | **Response 2 (Daily Tracker)**  | **Notes**                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No Response                   | Not applicable                  | Call not answered.                                               |
| Invalid                       | Not applicable                  | Number invalid/unreachable/wrong number.                         |
| Not Hiring                    | Not applicable                  | Company confirmed not hiring currently.                          |
| Already Connected             | Not applicable                  | Company already engaged via another coordinator/channel.         |
| Follow Up                     | Not applicable in Daily Tracker | Call back required; carried forward, not tracked further here.   |
| Invite Mail                   | Not applicable in Daily Tracker | Invite requested; JD/invite lifecycle tracked in Weekly Tracker. |
| Drive Scheduled               | Not applicable in Daily Tracker | Lifecycle progress tracked in Weekly Tracker.                    |
| Drive In Progress             | Not applicable in Daily Tracker | Lifecycle progress tracked in Weekly Tracker.                    |
| Drive Completed               | Not applicable in Daily Tracker | Lifecycle progress tracked in Weekly Tracker.                    |

Intelligent filtering still applies within Call Outcome selection where relevant statuses depend on context, but no Response 2 value is captured or stored in Module 03.

# 13\. Submit Day - Validation Rules

Validation before Submit Day is intentionally soft - it warns, but never blocks, submission:

- Start Time and End Time must be present for every worked row (enforced at the row level per Section 10.6).
- Call Outcome must be selected for every worked row.
- Comments are always optional.
- If Call Outcome = Invite Mail but the Email ID is missing, the coordinator may still submit the day. The system carries this forward as a soft reminder the next time the coordinator logs in, prompting them to supply the missing Email ID (one prompt/chance is given).

Example confirmation dialog:

- "68 rows completed. 2 companies require Email ID. You can submit now - these records will appear tomorrow as Pending Information." with Submit Anyway and Go Back options.

# 14\. Auto-Save, Manual Save & Submit Day

- Each row auto-saves as soon as it is completed (Call Outcome selected).
- A manual Save control (and Ctrl+S) is also available at any time.
- Submit Day is a distinct, final action performed once at the end of the working day, after all rows are saved.
- The bottom status bar always shows Auto Saved / Last Saved timestamp, row count, and current progress percentage, giving the coordinator confidence their work is not lost.

# 15\. Carry-Forward of Incomplete Contacts

- No Response and Follow Up contacts are not force-closed at Submit Day.
- When the coordinator opens the next day's tracker, these contacts are available to optionally continue.
- The coordinator may delete them from the new day's list or continue working them, entirely at their discretion, before adding fresh contacts for the new day.

# 16\. Daily Tracker UI Design

## 16.1 Top Section

- Tracker title (e.g. "July Tracker 2026"), coordinator name, and today's date.
- Today's call count and a visual progress indicator. There is no mandatory daily call target enforced by the system - 70 calls/day is an internal team guideline, and a positive-call-rate benchmark (20+/day) is also a guideline only, not a system-enforced rule.

## 16.2 Toolbar

- Load Contacts, Save, Submit Day, Refresh, Skip Selected, History, Filter, Search.

## 16.3 Live Statistics (KPI cards)

- Completed, Pending, Positive, No Response, Follow Up, Skipped - updating live as the coordinator works, without a separate dashboard page.

## 16.4 Daily Tracker Grid

- Columns as defined in Section 9, presented as a fast, keyboard-navigable Excel-style grid.

## 16.5 Bottom Status Bar

- Auto Saved / Last Saved time, total rows, currently selected row, and today's overall progress percentage.

## 16.6 Colour Coding

- Green = Positive, Blue = In Progress, Orange = Pending, Red = Critical, Grey = Inactive - applied consistently across the Daily Tracker, Weekly Tracker, Dashboard, Analytics, and Reports for a unified visual language.

# 17\. Role-Based Permission Matrix

| **Feature / Action**                                | **Coordinator** | **Team Leader** | **Administrator** |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------- | ----------------- |
| Load today's contacts (read-only picker)            | **Y**           | **Y**           | **Y**             |
| Enter/edit call data in own tracker                 | **Y**           | **N/A**         | **N/A**           |
| View another coordinator's daily tracker            | **N**           | **Y**           | **Y**             |
| Skip a contact for the day                          | **Y**           | **Y**           | **Y**             |
| Submit Day                                          | **Y**           | **N/A**         | **N/A**           |
| Add new contact synced to Master Database           | **Y**           | **Y**           | **Y**             |
| View aggregate daily statistics across coordinators | **N**           | **Y**           | **Y**             |

# 18\. Integration With Other Modules

- Master Company Database (Module 02): supplies contacts via the read-only picker; new contacts discovered during calls are added there first, then synced back into the Daily Tracker.
- Weekly Tracker (Module 04): receives positive outcomes automatically after Submit Day, carrying Serial No., Company Name, and Status; Role and CDC fields are left blank for the Team Leader/coordinator to fill in later, alongside Company Type.

Architectural decision carried forward from this discussion: Daily Tracker = Daily Activity (what happened on today's call), Weekly Tracker = Placement Lifecycle (how a lead progresses over days or weeks after a positive call). Keeping these responsibilities separate keeps both modules simple, focused, and easier to maintain.

# 19\. Business Rules Summary

- The Daily Tracker always opens empty each day; the previous day is fully saved and submitted before a new day begins.
- Contacts are loaded only through the read-only Load Today's Contacts picker - never by typing or free-text search within the Daily Tracker.
- Coordinators choose their own working set of contacts at their own discretion; there is no system-assigned call order.
- A contact already completed with a final outcome should not be repeated the same day; Follow Up / No Response / Call Back contacts may legitimately be repeated.
- Start Time is manually entered (typed or via Spacebar/⏱ Now) and remains editable; End Time and Duration are always automatic and locked.
- Call Outcome is mandatory before a row is considered complete; Comments are always optional.
- Missing Email ID never blocks Submit Day; it is carried forward as a one-time reminder on next login.
- Skip removes a contact from today's tracker only - it never deletes the record from the Master Company Database.
- Only Call Outcome (not a secondary business status) is recorded in the Daily Tracker; all longer-term lifecycle statuses belong to the Weekly Tracker.

# 20\. Deferred / Out of Scope for v1.0

- Telephony-integrated, true talk-time measurement (system-verified call start/end at the carrier level) - out of scope; Duration in v1.0 is activity duration, not verified conversation time.
- Response 2 / secondary business status inside the Daily Tracker - intentionally removed and relocated to Module 04 - Weekly Tracker.
- Fixed daily call quotas or system-enforced positive-call targets - not implemented; guideline-only per current company policy.

# 21\. Conclusion

Module 03 is considered functionally complete (Version 1.0). The Daily Tracker is designed to feel like the Excel sheet coordinators already use, while behaving like an enterprise application underneath - with automatic time capture, duplicate prevention, soft validation, keyboard-first data entry, and automatic hand-off of positive outcomes to the Weekly Tracker. This module is the execution workspace of the system; Module 02 supports it silently in the background, and Module 04 will take over the longer-term placement lifecycle once a lead goes positive here.

# 22\. Next Module

Module 04 - Weekly Tracker: the operational planning board for the placement lifecycle after a positive call, covering Invite Sent, JD Requested/Received, Drive Scheduled, Drive In Progress, Interview Rounds, Awaiting Offers, and Drive Completed.
